summary: Introduces testing strategies for the applications Ansible deploys (not module development), noting Ansible's fail-fast, ordered, push-based design makes it easy to embed tests in playbooks to stop bad updates.
questions: How can I build tests into my Ansible deployments?
Can Ansible stop a failed update from rolling out to all servers?
Where are docs on testing Ansible modules versus testing my deployments?

answer_card.title: Testing deployments with Ansible
answer_card.answer_md:
Ansible is fail-fast and ordered, so you can embed tests directly in playbooks. Adding checks to your deployment workflow means fewer production surprises, and tests can stop a failed update from spreading across all hosts. Because it is push-based, you can easily run the same steps against localhost or test servers.

This is about testing what you deploy; module testing is covered in the Development docs.
